## Project overview

This project explores associations between HEXACO personality traits and
teamwork quality using questionnaire data.

It includes an analysis of observed questionnaire data and a Shiny app for
exploring observed relationships and comparing hypothetical team-formation
strategies. Simulated outcomes reflect model assumptions; they are not proven
effects or predictions for real teams.

## Data and scoring

The observed dataset contains questionnaire responses from 54 participants.
The raw file is stored at `data/HEXACO_TWQ_raw-data.csv`. The processing code
scores HEXACO and teamwork-quality dimensions from questionnaire items. The
`src/data_processing.R` script also creates the processed file used by the
standalone simulation. That script currently downloads the source data from
OSF, so processing it requires an internet connection.

```{r processing}
source("data_processing.R")
```

## Descriptive statistics and relationships

The analysis script summarizes the processed scores and creates the heatmap
and scatterplot shown below. It reads `data/processed_data.csv`.

```{r descriptive-analysis}
source("src/data_analysis.R")
knitr::kable(summary_table, row.names = FALSE,
             caption = "Descriptive statistics for HEXACO and teamwork-quality scores")
```

```{r correlation-heatmap, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/plot_heatmap.png")
```

The observed correlation between agreeableness and support is
`r round(cor(df$agreeableness, df$support, use = "complete.obs"), 2)`. These
correlations describe associations, not causal effects.

```{r relationship-scatterplot, out.width="100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/plot_scatter_agreeableness.png")
```

## Statistical analysis

The analysis below examines the association between agreeableness and reported
communication quality. The script loads the raw data from the `data/` folder,
creates the scores, fits the exploratory linear model, and prints its summary.

```{r analysis}
print(summary(model))
print(communication_plot)
```

The model is exploratory and does not account for participants belonging to
the same team. The sample is small, and the variables were selected after
examining correlations. Interpret the results accordingly; observed
associations do not establish causation.

## Simulation

The standalone `data_simulation.R` script generates hypothetical HEXACO
profiles and teamwork-quality outcomes using explicit assumptions. It reads
processed scores from `data/processed_data.csv`, uses shared calculations from
`simulation_core.R`, and writes its outputs to `simulated_data/`.

The current configuration creates 500 teams of four people for each of two
paired scenarios: low target diversity (0.20) and high target diversity (0.80).
The results below are from the latest files saved in `simulated_data/`. They
reflect the simulation assumptions and are not observed effects in real teams.

### Simulated teamwork-quality scores

```{r simulation-outcome-summary}
simulated_summary <- read.csv(
  "simulated_data/teamwork_quality_summary.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  simulated_summary[, c("Scenario", "outcome_label", "n_participants",
                        "mean_score", "sd_score")],
  digits = 2,
  col.names = c("Scenario", "Outcome", "Participants", "Mean", "SD"),
  caption = "Simulated teamwork-quality score summaries"
)
```

### Achieved diversity

This table compares the target within-team trait SD with the average SD
actually achieved in the generated teams.

```{r simulation-diversity-summary}
diversity_summary <- read.csv(
  "simulated_data/diversity_summary.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  diversity_summary[, c("Scenario", "trait_label", "target_sd",
                        "mean_achieved_sd", "sd_across_teams")],
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Scenario", "Trait", "Target SD", "Achieved mean SD",
                "SD across teams"),
  caption = "Target and achieved within-team trait diversity"
)
```

### Paired high-versus-low comparison

The simulation reuses paired draws across the low- and high-diversity scenarios.
The intervals describe variation across simulated teams under the selected
assumptions; they are not evidence about real-world effects.

```{r simulation-paired-summary}
paired_differences <- read.csv(
  "simulated_data/paired_team_level_differences.csv",
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(
  paired_differences[, c("outcome_label", "n_teams", "mean_difference",
                         "ci_low", "ci_high", "paired_cohens_dz")],
  digits = 3,
  col.names = c("Outcome", "Teams", "High minus low", "95% CI low",
                "95% CI high", "Paired effect size"),
  caption = "Paired team-level outcome differences"
)
```


### Simulation sanity checks

The project includes deterministic checks of the shared simulation logic. They
verify that Random, Balanced, and Similar assignments give every team the
requested number of members; that Balanced and Similar produce the expected
between-team variance ordering on a fixed example; and that zero composition
and diversity effects produce no strategy differences when residual draws are
shared.

```{r simulation-sanity-checks}
source("sanity_checks.R")
```

The variance ordering is checked on a fixed example so the result is
reproducible; a random simulation can occasionally show a different ordering
by chance.

## Interactive app

The Shiny app provides controls for exploring observed questionnaire data and
comparing simulated team-formation strategies. From the project root, launch it
with:

```{r launch-app, eval=FALSE}
shiny::runApp("Shiny_App.R")
```

The app's simulated-data view reads
`simulated_data/combined_individual_level_results.csv`. The interactive team
comparison also uses the shared calculations in `simulation_core.R`.

## Project files

- `data/` — raw and processed questionnaire data files.
- `figures/` — figures created by the observed-data analysis.
- `simulated_data/` — saved simulation datasets, summaries, diagnostics, and plots.
- `src/` — additional analysis scripts, including `data_analysis.R`.
- `data_processing.R` — exploratory analysis of the raw questionnaire data.
- `data_simulation.R` — standalone simulation script.
- `simulation_core.R` — shared simulation functions.
- `sanity_checks.R` — quick checks for team assignment and strategy outcomes.
- `Shiny_App.R` — interactive Shiny app.
- `main.Rmd` — this report.

## Limitations

The observed sample is small, and participants belong to existing teams.
Analyses should account for that grouping where appropriate. Observed
associations do not establish causation. Scoring choices and missing-response
handling should be checked against the questionnaire documentation.
Simulated results depend on assumptions and are not validated predictions of
real team performance.
